clue.text: Self-interested type takes hours to penetrate group of stars

indicators.note: one letter is to go right into the middle of the constellation's name, piercing it

parts.note: Cancer, the Crab, is a constellation of the zodiac

explanation.surface: An opportunist muscles in on a celebrity circle by putting in the hours.
explanation.definitionFit: An opportunist always out for personal gain is called a chancer in British slang.

clue.text: Harry and Henry nabbed by someone not in uniform

indicators.note: the letter is caught and held inside the word for a civilian

parts.note: a civvy is a civilian, someone out of military uniform
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Prince Harry and Prince Henry seized by a plain-clothes agent.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry is not the prince but a verb, to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry and to chivvy both mean to nag or pester someone persistently.

clue.text: Charm everyone with a flower

parts.note: all means everyone
a flower is something that flows, a river; the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Win everyone over with a bunch of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is the crossword pun for a river (something that flows); the Ure runs through North Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Allure is attractiveness or the power to entice, a synonym of charm.

clue.text: Remark about American university's dedication

indicators.note: the remark goes around the university's letters

parts.note: a comment is a remark
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: An observation praising the hard work of a US college.
explanation.definitionFit: Commitment is devotion to a cause, which is what dedication means.

clue.text: Rock band followed by American uncle telling folk stories

indicators.note: the band name comes first and the other piece follows it

parts.note: R.E.M. is an American rock band
US stands for American, as in the US

explanation.surface: A rock band and then an American relative who spins folk tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle Remus is the narrator of Joel Chandler Harris's collection of African-American folk tales.

clue.text: Employment in a bar makes one excited

indicators.note: the word for employment sits inside the letters for 'a bar'

parts.note: a rod is a bar of metal or wood
use is employment, as in 'put to employment'

explanation.surface: Getting a job in a pub gives someone a thrill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bar' looks like a pub, but it is a letter plus a metal rod; 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has been stirred up or stimulated is aroused, a close synonym of excited.

clue.text: Orchestra losing leader, a man very great and loyal

indicators.note: the orchestra's name drops its first letter

parts.note: the Hallé is a famous orchestra based in Manchester
a giant is a very great man

explanation.surface: An orchestra loses its conductor but a great man stays faithful.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hallé is Manchester's symphony orchestra; without H it gives ALLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegiant is an old word for loyal, owing allegiance.

clue.text: Binge in which Bess's partner loses head

indicators.note: the partner's name drops its opening letter

parts.note: Porgy and Bess is Gershwin's opera; Porgy is Bess's lover

explanation.surface: A wild party at which a man loses his head.
explanation.definitionFit: An orgy is a bout of excessive indulgence, which is what a binge is.

clue.text: Employees restricting production ultimately create deadlock

indicators.note: the employees hem in the other letters

parts.note: staff are employees

indicators.note: the final letter of production is taken

parts.note: to do is to make or create, as in 'do a drawing'

explanation.surface: Workers holding back output end up causing an impasse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restricting' is the container signal and 'ultimately' takes the final letter of production; 'create' for DO is loose (the printed clue had 'creating').
explanation.definitionFit: A standoff is a stalemate where neither side can win, a synonym of deadlock.

clue.text: Set off from school in the course of a particular day

indicators.note: the school sits within the day, as something happens in the course of it

parts.note: a date is a particular day
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: Pupils leave school during a particular day.
explanation.definitionFit: To detonate a bomb is to set it off, making it explode.

clue.text: Is priest or monk not entirely necessary for religion?

indicators.note: the holy man's title is cut short, its final letter dropped

parts.note: a lama is a Buddhist priest or monk in Tibet

explanation.surface: A question of whether clergy are really needed for faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Islam is the faith of Muslims, one of the major world religions.

clue.text: Little good in head worker — bad

indicators.note: the letter for good is placed inside the headland's name

parts.note: Malin Head is the northernmost point of Ireland, named in the shipping forecast
G is the short form, a little version, of good
the ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a minor talent in the boss's chair as no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is not a boss but MALIN, as in Malin Head, Ireland's northern tip and a shipping-forecast area.
explanation.definitionFit: Malignant describes something evil or harmful, so it serves for bad in the sense of wicked.

clue.text: Private viewing is flop, somehow never entertaining

indicators.note: the rearranged word holds the other letters inside it, as a host entertains guests
somehow says the letters of 'never' are arranged in some other way

parts.note: to sag is to flop or droop

explanation.surface: A critic sniffs that a gallery preview failed, though it never seemed to be fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges the letters of 'never' into VERNE, and 'entertaining' makes that hold the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A vernissage is the private preview of an art exhibition before its public opening.

clue.text: Place of iniquity after hint of ecstasy?

definitions.text: Place of iniquity after hint of ecstasy?

indicators.note: only the opening letter of ecstasy is taken, a mere hint of it

parts.note: a den of iniquity is a haunt of vice

explanation.surface: A vice haunt that follows a taste of bliss.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole, the clue describes the garden of Genesis: a place of bliss where sin followed.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the garden of paradise was the scene of the first sin, after its original bliss.

clue.text: Go with others abroad — gems found travelling

indicators.note: these letters move from place to place into a new order

explanation.surface: Head overseas with friends, and jewels turn up on the trip.
explanation.walkthrough: Go is the oriental board game, so 'Go with others' is a group of such games.
explanation.definitionFit: Go is a board game; together with others like it the plural answer covers the whole category.

clue.text: Lunatic put away — having admitted mistake, I succeeded

parts.note: mad means lunatic, crazy

indicators.note: the word for consuming lets other letters in, as a doorman admits guests

parts.note: to put away food is to eat it
a goof is a blunder or mistake

explanation.surface: A madman is locked up, owns up to an error, and claims a triumph anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having admitted' puts the mistake and I inside the word for put away, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a success of something is an idiom for having succeeded at it.

clue.text: Joy gets hold of Bill, maybe for protective cover

indicators.note: the joy word grips the bill inside it

parts.note: delight means joy
an ad, advertisement, is a bill or poster

explanation.surface: Someone happy gets their hands on a bill, perhaps to keep it safe.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlight is a protective shutter or plate fitted over a ship's porthole.

clue.text: Fighter discarded document apart from a page

indicators.note: the letters for a page are excluded from the document

parts.note: scrap paper is paper thrown away or used for rough notes
A plus P, the abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: A boxer is portrayed in a document that was thrown away, minus one page.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrapper is someone who fights or brawls readily.

clue.text: Son experienced hallucinations in the nude

parts.note: to trip is to hallucinate on drugs

explanation.surface: A son on drugs ends up running around naked.
explanation.definitionFit: Stripped means naked, having had one's clothes removed.

clue.text: Plant mat without colour

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the word for a mat goes round the colour

parts.note: a coaster is a small mat for a glass
a tone is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: A doormat or table mat lacking any colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking: CO-TONE-ASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Cotoneaster is a shrub of the rose family, grown for its berries.

clue.text: Shelter quietly demolished in naval battle

indicators.note: the quiet letter is knocked out of the battle's name

parts.note: Lepanto was the sea battle of 1571 between the Holy League and the Ottomans
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A refuge is quietly destroyed during a sea fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a simple shed or shelter built against a wall.

clue.text: Design fashionable accommodation for holiday-makers?

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
a tent is where campers stay; the question mark admits it is only one kind of holiday lodging

explanation.surface: Planning trendy lodging for tourists.
explanation.definitionFit: Intent is a purpose or plan, the sense of design in 'by design'.

clue.text: A symbol for unknown is accompanying it?

definitions.text: A symbol for unknown is accompanying it?

parts.note: x is the algebraic symbol for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: A maths question about whether an unknown symbol goes along with something.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes the x-axis: the line that goes with the unknown x on a graph.
explanation.definitionFit: On a graph each variable such as x has its own reference line, so the line goes along with the symbol.

clue.text: Legion ever on the move in something like khaki?

indicators.note: the letters of these words are moving around into a new order

explanation.surface: A Roman legion is on the march again, dressed in army drab.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive green is a dull brownish green colour close to khaki, used for military uniforms.

clue.text: As some disease gives you runs, you get medicinal bottle round

indicators.note: the bottle goes round the letter for runs

parts.note: a vial is a small bottle for medicine
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An illness gives you diarrhoea, so you get a bottle of medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs' looks like diarrhoea, but it is R, the cricket scorecard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A disease caused by a virus is described as viral.

clue.text: Star gets less than complete admiration

indicators.note: only a part from inside the word admiration is used

explanation.surface: A celebrity gets only partial praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Mira is a variable red giant in the constellation Cetus.

clue.text: Vocalist with bell conveying love with extra note

indicators.note: the bell word carries the other letters inside it

parts.note: a pinger is a device that rings like a bell, such as a kitchen timer
O is love, a zero score in tennis
PS, postscript, is a note added at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A singer with a bell sends a love letter with a postscript.
explanation.definitionFit: A pop singer performs popular music, so is a kind of vocalist.

clue.text: Rodents eating last bit of rotten food

indicators.note: the rodents take the letter inside them as if swallowing it

parts.note: mice are small rodents

indicators.note: only the final letter of rotten is used

explanation.surface: Rats or mice nibbling at the last scraps of something gone off.
explanation.definitionFit: Mince is minced meat, a staple food.

clue.text: Brilliant mathematician's angle, central feature of lecture

parts.note: the radian is a unit of angle used in mathematics

indicators.note: only the letter at the middle of lecture is taken

explanation.surface: A dazzling maths professor makes angles the core of a lecture.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiant means shining brightly, a synonym of brilliant.

clue.text: The French drink in bars to keep going

parts.note: la is the feminine form of 'the' in French
stout is a dark beer served in pubs

explanation.surface: A Frenchman drinking in pubs to keep himself going.
explanation.definitionFit: To last out is to endure or keep going to the end.
